name: Lois Frankel

items.text: Frankel was criticized over a $20,000 contribution to her 2012 congressional campaign from Digital Domain Media Group. It came about five months after the company won a downtown West Palm Beach project that included city incentives. Wikipedia says she responded by vowing to give the money to charity. No finding of wrongdoing was located.
items.why: A single large campaign gift raises a big-money question (criterion 3), but no official finding or record shows wrongdoing, and I could not read the original reporting.

for_review: I only reached Wikipedia for item 1. I could not open the original news report it cites, so the timing, the response and whether the $20,000 went to charity are unverified. Check FEC 2012 filings for the Digital Domain Media Group contribution and any refund or disbursement, plus the Palm Beach Post coverage. A related search found that Digital Domain later went bankrupt and that West Palm Beach had given the company $2 million (The Real Deal, 2012). I did not tie that to Frankel, and it is not part of the item. The owner-sites search (alexjoneslive.com, stewpeters.com, ryandawson.org, infowars.com) returned nothing about Frankel, so there is nothing to attribute. I did not weigh attendance, which is counted separately.
